title: Mushroom Emoji 🍄 Meaning: Mario, Shrooms, Cottagecore
description: The 🍄 mushroom emoji means Super Mario power-ups, psychedelic “shrooms,” and the cottagecore forest aesthetic. Find out which one a message is pointing to.
summary: The 🍄 mushroom emoji is a red toadstool with white spots. It references the Super Mario power-up, psychedelic mushrooms and trippy experiences, and a whimsical woodland aesthetic. It is also used for foraging and cooking, although the mushroom it depicts is poisonous.
meaning: The red cap with white dots is a fly agaric, the toadstool of European fairy tales, garden gnomes and Alice in Wonderland. It is also, to anyone who has held a game controller, the Super Mushroom that makes Mario grow. Gamers use 🍄 for the franchise, for Mario Kart speed boosts and for “powering up” in a general sense, such as coffee before a long shift.

Among adults the emoji very often means psilocybin mushrooms. “Shrooms” have their own culture of festival trips, microdosing and, increasingly, clinical research and decriminalization debates, and 🍄 is the obvious symbol for all of it. With swirls, stars, aliens or melting faces it describes a psychedelic experience. Sellers and buyers use it as code. By extension it tags anything surreal, colorful or dreamlike.

A gentler meaning comes from internet aesthetics. Cottagecore, goblincore and fairycore all celebrate moss, frogs, snails and toadstools, and the mushroom is close to a logo for them. It appears on handmade jewelry, embroidery, tattoos and bedroom decor posts. Foragers and cooks use it literally for wild or store-bought fungi, and a brown mushroom emoji was later added for more realistic kitchen use.

contexts.label: In gaming
contexts.body: It is Mario shorthand. Players use it for Nintendo news, speedruns, Mario Kart items and the character Toad, whose head is a mushroom cap. “Need a 🍄” means needing a boost or an extra life. The reference is so well known that non-gamers understand it.

contexts.label: In texting
contexts.body: Between adults discussing weekend plans, festivals or “a trip,” it probably means psychedelics. In a message about dinner, it is risotto or pizza toppings. From someone with a woodland-themed profile, it is decoration. Occasionally it is a crude joke about anatomy, which the tone will make plain.

contexts.label: On TikTok and Instagram
contexts.body: Mushroom-themed art, crochet, thrifted decor and outfit videos use it as an aesthetic tag, often with 🐸, 🌿 and 🍂. Foraging creators use it for identification videos. Wellness accounts use it for functional mushroom products like lion’s mane coffee. Psychedelic content tends to pair it with ✨ or 🌀.

contexts.label: In captions
contexts.body: Autumn walks produce plenty of toadstool photos, and the emoji labels them. Food posts use it for anything mushroom-based. Fantasy and fairy-tale imagery uses it for scale and whimsy, suggesting a tiny world on the forest floor where gnomes and fairies might live.

combos.meaning: Mushrooms as a pizza topping or ingredient.

confusedWith.difference: 🌿 is a green sprig that often signals cannabis. The mushroom signals psychedelics. In drug-related messages they refer to different substances, and people sometimes list both.

🌵 is a desert plant used for dry places and prickly personalities. It occasionally hints at peyote or mescaline, another psychedelic, but that is rare. The mushroom is the standard emoji for hallucinogens.
💥 is an explosion burst. People who want a “mushroom cloud” sometimes combine the two, but the mushroom alone almost never means a nuclear blast. It refers to the fungus, the game or the drug.

avoid: Avoid using it casually with coworkers or family if you do not want to imply drug use.
Do not use it as a guide to what is edible; the red-and-white mushroom shown is toxic.
Skip it as an insult about someone’s body, which is crude and widely recognized.
design: Apple, Google, Samsung and most others draw a fly agaric: a rounded red cap with white spots on a thick white stem. Some designs add a frilly ring on the stalk or a patch of grass. Google’s cap has at times been more orange-red. The image matches the Super Mario mushroom closely, which reinforces the gaming meaning. A separate brown mushroom emoji now exists for ordinary edible varieties.

faqs.a: Usually psychedelic mushrooms, also called shrooms or magic mushrooms, or the experience of taking them. It can also mean something trippy and surreal. In gaming circles it is slang for a power-up, taken from Super Mario.

faqs.q: What does 🍄 mean from a girl?
faqs.a: She may love the cottagecore look, be a Nintendo fan, be cooking, or be referring to psychedelics. Check her other emojis: frogs and leaves suggest aesthetics, stars and swirls suggest a trip. It is not a flirting signal.

faqs.q: What does 🍄 mean from a guy?
faqs.a: Most likely gaming or shrooms, depending on the conversation. If he is planning a festival or camping weekend, it is the drug. Some men use it self-deprecatingly or as an insult about male anatomy, a meaning popularized by tabloid stories.

The species it portrays, the fly agaric, is toxic and can cause serious illness. It is a storybook toadstool, not a cooking mushroom. People still use the emoji for edible mushrooms, and a brown mushroom emoji was added later to represent those.

It appears in three main communities: cottagecore and goblincore creators who love toadstool imagery, foragers and cooks, and people discussing psychedelics or microdosing. The video’s subject will show which one applies.
